sources.shortCitation: Jean Choux on sound cinema — Excelsior
sources.fullCitation: “Les metteurs en scène devant l’évolution du cinéma: Le cinéma, depuis qu’il parle, fait à l’homme et à ses propos une part exhorbitante, déclare M. Jean Choux.” Excelsior (Paris), 25 December 1936, p. 4. With a photograph captioned “Jean Choux dirigeant l’exécution d’une prise de vues.” Bibliothèque nationale de France / RetroNews.
sources.title: Les metteurs en scène devant l’évolution du cinéma: Jean Choux
sources.creator: Jean Choux (interviewee)
sources.researchNote: The photograph carries no photographer’s or agency’s credit, unlike the studio portraits the paper usually printed. It shows the director at work rather than posed: he is crouching beside the camera, giving a signal, with the operator behind him. The interview belongs to a series in which directors were asked what the coming of sound had changed; Choux argues that speech has given man and his words a disproportionate share of the screen.

media.title: Jean Choux directing a take — Excelsior, 25 December 1936
media.description: Press photograph of the director Jean Choux crouching beside the camera during a take, published with the interview series “Les metteurs en scène devant l’évolution du cinéma”.
media.altText: Jean Choux crouching beside a film camera on a tripod, one hand raised in a signal, with a camera operator standing behind him.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. The photograph is printed without a photographer’s or agency’s credit and is therefore treated as an anonymous work published in 1936, for which the seventy-year term of protection in France ran out at the end of 2006.
media.publicCaption: Jean Choux directing a take, from the series of interviews with directors on the evolution of cinema published in Excelsior on 25 December 1936.
media.publicCreditLine: Photographer uncredited; Excelsior, 25 December 1936, p. 4. RetroNews, Bibliothèque nationale de France.
